title: Josh Comeau
tagline: Interactive CSS and React essays that make hard ideas click.
note: The flexbox and rendering-performance posts are canonical — assign them before any debate about layout. Steal the teaching method: every abstract idea anchored to a widget you can poke.

title: Overreacted
tagline: Dan Abramov's React mental models in plain language.
note: Read the effects and closures pieces twice. Few writers separate what React does from what you should do as cleanly — required reading before arguing about hooks.

title: Emil Kowalski
tagline: Animation and interaction craft, every post shipping a demo.
note: The reference for UI that feels physical. Study how each post isolates one interaction variable — duration, spring, gesture — until the right value is undeniable.

title: Rauno Freiberg
tagline: Short, sharp notes on interface details most teams never notice.
note: Proof that taste is attention: tiny observations about spacing, timing, and states that compound into obviously better interfaces. Read in one sitting.

title: Lee Robinson
tagline: Frontend performance and shipping notes from Vercel's VP of product.
note: The Web Vitals writing is relentlessly practical — what to measure, what to fix first. Steal the prioritization: performance budgets before performance tricks.

title: Delba
tagline: DX engineering notes on caching, RSC, and the details behind the docs.
note: Where Next.js caching finally makes sense. Read the caching posts before touching a fetch call — they explain the why that the reference docs assume.

title: Robin Rendle
tagline: Design criticism with a long memory, from type history to interfaces.
note: Connects today's interfaces to centuries of typographic craft. Read when your work feels ahistorical — it cures the blank-canvas amnesia of framework churn.

title: Anthony Fu
tagline: Open-source velocity in public: tools, UnoCSS, and maintainer craft.
note: A masterclass in building in the open — small modules, fast iteration, honest changelogs. Steal the release cadence and the way each tool does exactly one thing.

title: Vercel Blog
tagline: Engineering write-ups behind Next.js and the platform.
note: The launch posts double as positioning lessons: each one frames a technical decision as a user outcome. Read for the infrastructure, study for the communication.

title: Figma Blog
tagline: Design-tooling thinking from the source, plus Config talk recaps.
note: Where design engineering direction gets announced first — variables, Dev Mode, code connect. Skim monthly to stay ahead of the Figma-to-code curve.

title: Linear Blog
tagline: Opinionated product engineering: quality, craft, and saying no.
note: The best corporate blog on saying no — to features, to speed, to mediocrity. The quality and method posts are a playbook for small teams with high standards.

title: Nielsen Norman Group Articles
tagline: Evidence over opinion for UX decisions — the citation that ends debates.
note: When a stakeholder wants a clever interaction, answer with research. The form and navigation studies are the highest-leverage bookmarks a designer can hold.

title: Dense Discovery
tagline: Weekly design, tech, and sustainability curation with actual taste.
note: The closest existing model to this library's voice — selective, opinionated, calmly written. Study the issue structure: few links, real context, zero hype.

title: Bytes
tagline: JavaScript news with jokes that land, three times a week.
note: The fastest way to stay current on the JS ecosystem without doomscrolling. The humor is load-bearing — it makes release notes memorable.

title: CSS Weekly
tagline: One CSS email, zero fluff — the archives double as a curriculum.
note: Read back through a year of archives and you'll have covered the whole modern CSS surface. The signal-to-noise ratio other newsletters should envy.

title: Frontend Focus
tagline: Cooper Press's curated frontend links — broad without being shallow.
note: The weekly scan for everything frontend: browser news, techniques, tools. Skim the headlines, deep-dive one link — that's the whole workflow.

title: Sidebar
tagline: Five human-picked design links a day, running since 2012.
note: The longevity is the endorsement — over a decade of daily curation without diluting. Proof that a small, consistent editorial habit compounds.

title: Smashing Magazine
tagline: Long-form front-end with a high editorial bar.
note: The accessibility and CSS archives are deep enough to be a reference library on their own. When you need the definitive article on a technique, check here first.

title: CSS for JavaScript Developers
tagline: The course that makes experienced JS developers stop fearing CSS.
note: Rebuilds CSS from the mental model up instead of property by property. The module on rendering and layout alone justifies it for any React developer.

title: Learn Web Development
tagline: Google's free, structured, current courses — the CSS and forms paths first.
note: The rare free resource with professional structure. Assign the CSS and forms paths to anyone onboarding into frontend; they're better than most paid courses.
